question: What is Zipher?
answer:
A privacy-first wallet built around one idea: you should never need more than a single input.

Zipher is a Zcash wallet where you type what you want — send, swap, bet, pay — and the app handles the rest. An on-device AI parses your intent. You confirm before anything irreversible.

For agents and developers, the same Rust engine powers zipher-cli and an MCP server with 29 tools.

Open source. No accounts. No telemetry. Keys never leave your device.

question: How is my money private?
answer:
Every transaction is shielded by default — amount, sender, and recipient are hidden on-chain using zero-knowledge proofs. Not a mixer. Not optional. Mathematically enforced.

Zipher has no backend. It connects to public lightwalletd servers for chain data only. Your keys live in the iOS Keychain, derived briefly in RAM, wiped on lock.

When a payment arrives, Zipher detects it locally by decrypting raw mempool transactions — your viewing keys never leave the device.

question: Is it safe?
answer:
Your seed lives in platform secure storage — iOS Keychain, Android Keystore. It enters RAM only to sign, then gets wiped. Every destructive action requires explicit confirmation.

The entire codebase is public. Zipher has not been formally audited yet — use the beta with caution and don't store more than you're willing to lose.

Back up your recovery phrase. If you lose it, no one — including us — can recover your funds.

question: Where do I download it?
answer:
iOS: open beta on TestFlight. Android: open testing on Google Play.

Install, create a wallet, and you're ready.

Agents & developers: npm install -g @cipherpay/zipher-cli — same Rust engine as the mobile app, headless.

question: Is it open source?
answer:
Yes — MIT licensed on GitHub: atmospherelabs-dev/zipher-app.

Flutter UI, Rust engine (sync, send, Polymarket, EVM swaps, voting proofs), zipher-cli, and zipher-mcp-server. We do not ask for trust. We show our work.

question: What is the agent wallet?
answer:
Zipher without a UI — a local-first Zcash light client for AI agents and automation.

Runs on a laptop, $5 VPS, or Raspberry Pi. Syncs in minutes via lightwalletd — no full node, no cloud custody. OWS encrypted vault (AES-256-GCM + scrypt) stores the mnemonic; process hardening disables core dumps at startup.

zipher-cli: two-step send (propose → confirm), NEAR Intents swaps, Polymarket, x402/MPP paywalls, daemon mode with kill switch. zipher-mcp-server: 29 tools over stdio for Claude, Cursor, and any MCP client.

Spending policy (per-tx caps, daily limits, allowlist, approval thresholds) and audit log on every action.

question: What is zipher-cli?
answer:
Headless Zcash light wallet — same Rust engine as the mobile app.

zipher wallet init              # OWS encrypted vault
zipher --human balance          # shielded balance
zipher --human polymarket list  # prediction markets
zipher serve                    # x402 pay-per-call HTTP API

Install: npm install -g @cipherpay/zipher-cli
Includes zipher-mcp-server. Keys stay on your machine.

question: Can an AI agent use this?
answer:
Yes. zipher-mcp-server exposes 29 tools over stdio — wallet status, propose/confirm send, shield, swaps, x402 payments, Polymarket, market research.

The server holds the seed in memory after unlock; tools never accept seed as an argument. Policy engine enforces limits before any signature. Transactions above approval_threshold return APPROVAL_REQUIRED — human-in-the-loop by design.

Mobile uses on-device SmolLM2 for intent parsing. Headless agents wire MCP into Claude, Cursor, or custom orchestrators.

question: How is this different from other wallets?
answer:
Most wallets are dashboards — tabs, forms, settings menus. Zipher bets on one input.

Type what you want. The wallet figures out the chain, the address format, the fee, the confirmation. You approve.

Privacy is not a feature toggle — Zcash shielded by default. And the same Rust engine that powers your phone also runs headless for AI agents, with spending policy, audit logs, and approval gates built in.

question: What can Action do?
answer:
Action is Zipher's conversational interface — and the direction every wallet should go. Instead of navigating screens, you describe what you want.

"send 5 zec to alice" · "swap 0.1 eth to zec" · "bet $20 on trump wins" · "pay this invoice"

The app parses intent using an on-device AI model. You see a confirmation with all details before anything signs. No surprises.

Action is live in the beta alongside the classic wallet view. Over time, it becomes the whole UI.
